opening::op4.text: Summer in Shiomi Town always ends slowly; the sea wind carries July all the way into late August.

opening::op6.text: On the second-to-last day of August, an unsigned letter appeared in my mailbox. One line only: before dawn, the old pier.

lake-meeting::b4.text: 5:40 in the morning. The mist had not lifted. Dew sat on the old pier planks, quieter underfoot than I remembered.

lake-meeting::b6.speaker: Makoto
lake-meeting::b6.text: This early? Umiya opens at seven. Even the boiler is still cold.

lake-meeting::b7.speaker: Lin Cheng
lake-meeting::b7.text: Makoto? What are you doing here?

lake-meeting::b8.speaker: Makoto
lake-meeting::b8.text: Helping Grandpa with the nets. You're the one holding a letter for ages. Waiting for someone?

lake-meeting::b9.speaker: Lin Cheng
lake-meeting::b9.text: ...Yeah. Someone I haven't spoken to in years.

lake-meeting::b10.speaker: Makoto
lake-meeting::b10.text: Good luck, then. If she doesn't show, come in for something hot. I'll sneak you an extra ice cube.

lake-meeting::b12.text: At six sharp, footsteps came through the mist. Unhurried, light, exactly as I remembered.

lake-meeting::b15.speaker: Lin Cheng
lake-meeting::b15.text: The letter said "miss today and you'll never see it again." Who would dare skip it?

lake-meeting::b16.speaker: Su Rui
lake-meeting::b16.text: That wasn't an exaggeration. There's a meteor shower tonight. The next one visible from Shiomi is eleven years away.

lake-meeting::b18.title: How do you answer her invitation?
options: Ask why she left back then

pier-talk::pt2.text: They sat on the pier until the mist cleared. Su Rui talked about her years away, then stopped mid-sentence.

pier-talk::pt3.speaker: Su Rui
pier-talk::pt3.text: The truth is, I left because I'd been admitted to a school far away, and my family couldn't even pay the rent. I didn't want anyone to see me cry over that.

pier-talk::pt4.speaker: Lin Cheng
pier-talk::pt4.text: You could have told us. Any of us would have helped.

pier-talk::pt5.speaker: Su Rui
pier-talk::pt5.text: I know. So saying it now isn't too late.

pier-talk::pt8.text: She smiled and changed the subject. Some words, it seemed, she wanted to keep a while longer.

old-school::school2.text: They walked the embankment to the abandoned elementary school. The iron gate had rusted shut and let out a long cry when pushed.

old-school::school3.speaker: Su Rui
old-school::school3.text: This is where the club held its last event. You wrote on the back of that group photo for me.

old-school::school4.speaker: Lin Cheng
old-school::school4.text: "Before summer ends, we watch the stars together one more time." Terrible handwriting. You actually kept it?

old-school::school5.speaker: Su Rui
old-school::school5.text: It's been in my pencil case ever since. That's why, coming back this time, you were the first person I thought of.

night-mail::nm3.text: At night a few lamps lit the pier. Makoto carried out folding chairs from the shop and declared that nobody was allowed to help before the shower began.

night-mail::nm5.speaker: Makoto
night-mail::nm5.text: The chairs are for you two. The cocoa is on me. Consider it thanks for being regulars.

night-mail::nm6.speaker: Lin Cheng
night-mail::nm6.text: Thanks, Makoto. I'll bring you some oranges from home.

night-mail::nm9.text: When the first meteor crossed the sea, the mist was gone for good. The stars fell into the water, as if someone had turned the whole sky upside down.

night-mail::nm10.title: What do you want to say tonight?

ending-star::es1.speaker: Lin Cheng
ending-star::es1.text: Su Rui. Eleven years from now, same place, same shower.

ending-star::es2.speaker: Su Rui
ending-star::es2.text: Deal. This time I'll write the letter first.

ending-star::es3.text: The stars sank into the sea one by one. Summer finally began to end.

ending-echo::ee1.text: Neither of them said a word. The waves pushed in, layer by layer, then pulled back out.

ending-echo::ee2.speaker: Su Rui
ending-echo::ee2.text: ...Even if you don't say it, I know what you want to say.

ending-echo::ee3.speaker: Lin Cheng
ending-echo::ee3.text: Then next time. We have eleven years, after all.

ending-echo::ee4.text: After the last meteor fell, light lingered on the sea. Some words keep, like echoes of a sea of stars.
